_README: The extreme-leg bot. IT IS ON THE BENCH: account is null, so it trades nothing, the boot sequence skips it and the runner refuses to start it. It exists so that putting it on an account is something Aaron does from the command center (Bots -> Accounts -> Add bot) rather than a code change. READ _NOT_ON_AN_ACCOUNT_YET AND _timeframe BEFORE ASSIGNING IT. This file is the ONLY thing that decides which terminal, account, symbol and strategy VERSION this bot trades -- nothing is read from strategies/python/extreme_leg/config.py, so lab experiments cannot reach it. No secrets here: the MT5 password is in algos/credentials.json under mt5_accounts, keyed by the account number it is assigned to.
_NOT_ON_AN_ACCOUNT_YET: TWO things must happen before this bot is assigned, and the first one is an ORDERING TRAP that fails loudly the wrong way round. (1) sos_fade_demo must move from exec_risk_pct 10.0 to 5.0 FIRST. The Command Center refuses any write where the shares on an account sum past its cap, so assigning this bot at 5% while the sibling states 10% against a 10% cap is refused at the moment of assignment -- 10 + 5 > 10. (2) It is UNPROMOTED (strategy_source_hash empty), so it would import from the repo working tree rather than a frozen snapshot. Promote it before it ever runs. WARNING - RULE 9: nothing in this package has been near a broker. Its live seams and the bridge's market-entry path are both tested and neither has executed once. See docs/EXTREME_LEG_BOT_PLAN.md section 4.3 for the live proving period, which is the only thing that closes that gap. WARNING - b_leg_demo is also benched and still states 10.0; the same share rule applies to it, and the three-way split is an open decision rather than arithmetic that already works.
_timeframe: M5, AND GETTING THIS WRONG FAILS SILENTLY -- it is the one field here that produces a bot which runs, logs cleanly and simply never trades. This strategy measures its trigger on 5-minute bars and builds its 15-minute half IN CODE from them. Hand it M15 and the trigger series and the target series become the same series, so there is no trade left to take. That looks exactly like a quiet market: no error, no refusal code, no alert. Every figure this bot has -- 113 trades / +58.53R over 470,995 bars, 2020-01-01 to 2026-08-23 -- was measured on M5, and its own lab entry declares suggested_bar_value 5. The same trap is recorded in backtest/tools/overlap_audit.py, which had to override the shared frame for this bot for the same reason.
_magic: 770117, one above b_leg_demo's 770116 and two above sos_fade_demo's 770115. live_config._assert_magic_is_unique REFUSES to start two bots sharing a magic on ONE account: every read in mt5_ops.py filters by it, so two bots sharing one would each read the OTHER's orders as their own -- cancel them, ratchet their stops, book their fills. The guard is per ACCOUNT and exempts a benched bot, so it enforces nothing today; the number is chosen now so that assigning this bot is never blocked by it.
_warmup_bars: 15,000 M5 bars = 52 calendar days, which is the SAME calendar warm-up sos_fade_demo gets from its 5,000 M15 bars. MEASURED FLOOR, not a guess: 1,008 bars (3.5 days). The probe replayed 12 quarterly start dates from 2022-04 to 2026-05, judging the 30 days after each, and compared a short run-up's decisions against a 20,000-bar reference -- 34 reference trades, and 1,008 / 2,016 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 15,000 all reproduce the reference everywhere while 504 does not (it diverges at 2025-12-23). WARNING - the FIRST version of that probe fingerprinted entry_index, a bar number local to each run's start, so every run-up disagreed with every other and it read exactly like an engine that never warms; and its first window held only 2 trades, which cannot separate warm from cold at all. A run-up is compared on decisions -- direction, times, prices, stop distance, R -- and never on bar numbers or dollar fields, because a longer run-up books more prior trades onto the emulator's compounding balance and moves every size legitimately. WARNING - 34 trades over 12 windows, with exactly ONE window separating the shortest run-up, so treat 1,008 as a floor with wide error bars. 15,000 is ~15x it and costs a few seconds at startup, which is why it is set generously rather than at the measured edge.
_account_risk_cap_pct: 10.0, matching the account this bot is intended for (700152905). It is the ACCOUNT-level ceiling on open risk across EVERY bot and every hand trade, measured to each position's CURRENT broker-side stop; exec_risk_pct is per-TRADE and sits under it. On a benched bot this field describes nothing -- there is no account for a ceiling to describe, and live_config._assert_account_cap_agrees exempts the bench -- but every bot on one account must state the SAME value or none of them will start, so it is set to what the account already carries. Do not set it by hand as part of an assignment; set it on Bots -> Accounts, which writes it to every bot on the account at once. WARNING - it REFUSES an order that does not fit and never shrinks one, which is the opposite of backtest/portfolio/. The shrink that keeps both books holding the same trade happens one layer earlier, in this strategy's own sizing at request_fill, before any order exists.
_exec_risk_pct: 5.0, which is the strategy's own shipped default AND Aaron's half of the split ('extreme will be 5% and sos fade will be 5%', 2026-09-03) -- they agree, so nothing is overridden here. Two shares of 5 sum to the 10% account cap exactly, so each bot can hold one full-size trade and the budget is fully allocated. WARNING - the sibling states 10.0 today and moving it is step one of the ordering trap in _NOT_ON_AN_ACCOUNT_YET. WARNING - this is the ONE runtime-reloadable field, so once this bot is running it reaches it on the next VPS git pull with no promote and no restart, applied at the next moment it is FLAT. WARNING - the 113-trade / +58.53R history was measured at 5.0, so this is the configuration every published figure for this bot describes.
_strategy_params: All 26 fields of ExtremeLegConfig, DUMPED from the dataclass rather than transcribed -- a hand-copied set is how a live bot ends up trading a value nobody chose, which is the rule b_leg_demo's own config already states. Exactly ONE is overridden and it is a fact about the broker rather than about the strategy: symbol XAUUSD.p, PU Prime's own gold string. point_value 1.0 and the 100oz contract already match this terminal, checked against both sibling configs. WARNING - there is no fill_model field on this config and none should be added here: bridge.assert_supported reads it defensively and gets 'bar', which is the only value the live path accepts. WARNING - skip_transitioning is ON, and it is the market-condition refusal NO PARITY GATE CAN EVER COVER -- it reads engines/regime/ and the Pine has no such engine, so compare_extreme_leg.py forces it OFF and compares the shared logic. The shipped bot takes FEWER trades than any green gate has ever checked. WARNING - use_breakeven is OFF and min_r is 2.0; both are shipped defaults and neither has been swept on this bot. WARNING - THERE IS NO account_profile HERE AND ADDING ONE STOPS THE BOT DEAD. ExtremeLegConfig does not declare that field, and runner._build_strategy REFUSES any strategy_params key the config class does not have -- 'they would be ignored, so the bot would trade settings you did not choose'. The 2026-09-04 assignment from Bots -> Accounts wrote account_profile puprime_ecn into this block because the account registry records one, and the bot then connected to the broker and refused to start on every attempt. It is written unconditionally by bot_accounts.plan_assignment, which reads the field off the ACCOUNT and never asks whether the receiving strategy declares it -- true for sos_fade and b_leg, false here. Do not re-add it, and re-check this block after any move between accounts.
_telegram: Both empty = the shared token and group from algos/credentials.json. Set telegram_chat_id to give this bot its own feed; set telegram_token_key (a KEY NAME in credentials.json, never a token) to give it its own Telegram identity.
_mt5_path: The MT5_FFT terminal, matching the two sibling bots. It is a placeholder while this bot is benched -- assigning it to an account ADOPTS that account's terminal path, because the terminal has to be logged into the account the bot claims to trade and only the bots already on it know which one that is.
_broker_tz_offsets: '2,3' std,dst hours ahead of UTC, copied from the sibling bots on the SAME broker and server -- it is a fact about PUPrime-Demo's server clock, not about a bot. The +3 half was MEASURED off the terminal's tick clock on 2026-07-31; the winter +2 is inferred from PU Prime's published schedule and is still UNVERIFIED. Re-measure with backtest/tools/compare_feeds.py after the November changeover: a wrong offset shifts every session boundary this strategy sweeps, and nothing downstream can detect it.
